name: Champion of Hecate
body:
Champions of Hecate, also known as Champions of the Moon and Magic, are dedicated to keeping magic alive and fighting the misguided belief that the use of witchcraft is inherently evil. These champions study beneficial herbs for their medicinal properties and patrol the roads to keep travelers safe (especially at nighttime when it’s most dangerous).

Background. Most Champions of Hecate began their careers as warriors or priestesses serving the temple. A few recruits are rogues with magical aptitude. Ancestries. Hecate’s followers are usually human, though giant kin and nymphs are also found among their ranks. Homeland. Many Champions of Hecate are from Anatolia, Thrace, Thessaly, and Magna Graecia. A few others come from Phoenicia and Illyria. Rarely are Hecate’s followers gathered from lands further away such as Persia, Kemet, Rome, and Carthage. Role. Champions of Hecate combine magic and martial skills, bringing many surprises and options to a battle. They may also serve as healers or escorts into dangerous lands. The champion’s enhanced spell list grants them additional flexibility in a support role as well. Religion. Champions of Hecate are always devoted to Hecate and her doctrine. This doesn’t preclude champions from honoring or worshipping other deities, but it does mean they hold Hecate above all others. Alignment. Champions of Hecate follow a strict code of secrecy, supplication, and respect. Their goddess emphasizes the rhythmic, cyclical, and magical aspects of life. For these reasons Champions of Hecate must be some form of Neutral alignment and cannot be Chaotic Evil, Chaotic Good, Lawful Evil, or Lawful Good. Adventures. Champions of Hecate adventure to serve their goddess and temple. They might be diplomats, covert agents, or security forces. They may be sent to help govern Byzantium or one of the smaller towns in the area. They are also responsible for serving the satellite temples throughout Magna Graecia and could be assigned to any temple between Trinakria and Persia. In these temples, they pursue the cult’s myriad and ambiguous objectives.

Sacred Promises

The following are the sacred promises made by a Champion of the Moon and Magic:

Protection… I will be vigilant at the gates, protecting cities and homes from outside aggression and restless spirits. I will escort pilgrims on their journeys to holy sites, caravans on their delivery routes, and travelers to their destinations.
Practitioners… work wonders with magic. I will support the practice of witchcraft and defend it from criticism.
Requirements

To qualify to become a Champion of Hecate, a character must fulfill all the following criteria.

Base Attack Bonus: +3
Skills: Knowledge (arcana) 3 ranks, Knowledge (religion) 3 ranks
Alignment: Chaotic Neutral, Neutral Good, Lawful Neutral, True Neutral, or Neutral Evil only.
Class skills

The Champion of Hecate’s class skills are Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Handle Animal (Cha), Heal (Wis), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (arcana) (Int), Knowledge (religion) (Int), Profession (Wis), Ride (Dex), Sense Motive (Wis), and Spellcraft (Int).

Skill Ranks at Each Level: 4 + Int modifier

Class features

All of the following are class features of the Champion of Hecate.

Prolific Magic: Champions of the Moon and Magic focus more on magic and less on martial training. At 1st level, these champions gain the Base Attack Bonus progression and Spell Progression of an Inquisitor. Charisma is still the Champion’s Spellcasting ability modifier, and like a typical champion, she must prepare her spells in advance. This alters base attack bonus and spells.

Smite Enemy (Su)

A Champion of Hecate may attempt to smite a favored enemy with one normal melee attack. She adds her Charisma bonus (if any) to her attack roll and deals 2 extra points of damage per champion level. If the champion accidentally smites a creature that is not a favored enemy, the smite has no effect, but the smite ability is still used. Champions may use this ability once per day per champion level, but never more than once per round.

Divine Grace

At 2nd level, a champion gains a bonus equal to her Charisma bonus (if any) on all Saving Throws.

Lay Hands: Beginning at 2nd level, a champion can heal wounds (her own or those of others) by touch. Each day she can use this ability a number of times equal to 1/2 her champion level plus her Charisma modifier. With one use of this ability, a champion can heal 1d6 hit points of damage for every two champion levels she possesses. Using this ability is a standard action, unless the champion targets herself, in which case it is a swift action. Despite the name of this ability, a champion only needs one free hand to use this ability.

Alternatively, a champion can use this healing power to deal damage to undead creatures, dealing 1d6 points of damage for every two levels the champion possesses. Using lay on hands in this way requires a successful melee touch attack and doesn’t provoke an attack of opportunity. Undead do not receive a saving throw against this damage.

Aura of Courage (Su)

At 3rd level, a champion is immune to fear (magical or otherwise). Each ally within 10 feet of her gains a +4 morale bonus on saving throws against fear effects. This ability functions only while the champion is conscious, not if she is unconscious or dead.

Divine Health (Ex)

At 3rd level, a champion is immune to all diseases, including supernatural and magical diseases, including mummy rot.

Mercy (Su)

At 3rd level, and every three levels thereafter, a champion can select one mercy. Each mercy adds an effect to the champion’s lay on hands ability. Whenever the champion uses lay on hands to heal damage to one target, the target also receives the additional effects from all of the mercies possessed by the champion. A mercy can remove a condition caused by a curse, disease, or poison without curing the affliction. Such conditions return after 1 hour unless the mercy actually removes the affliction that causes the condition.

At 3rd level, the champion can select from the following initial mercies.

Deceived: The target can immediately attempt a new saving throw to disbelieve any ongoing illusions that it failed to disbelieve within the last minute.
Fatigued: The target is no longer fatigued.
Riled: The champion’s lay on hands also acts as calm emotions, but only for the purpose of suppressing morale bonuses (such as from the rage spell) and emotion effects that aren’t fear effects. Use the champion’s level as the caster level.
Shaken: The target is no longer shaken.
Sickened: The target is no longer sickened.

At 6th level, a champion adds the following mercies to the list of those that can be selected.

Dazed: The target is no longer dazed.
Diseased: The champion’s lay on hands ability also acts as remove disease, using the champion’s level as the caster level.
Enfeebled: The champion dispels any magical effects that are reducing one of the target’s ability scores (champion’s choice).
Haunted: The champion’s lay on hands also acts as protection from evil, but only for the purpose of allowing a new saving throw against enchantment (charm) and enchantment (compulsion) effects, making the target immune to any attempts to possess or exercise mental control over the target, or preventing a life force from controlling the target (all as described in the second effect of protection from evil). Use the champion’s level as the caster level.
Staggered: The target is no longer staggered, unless the target is at exactly 0 hit points.
Targeted: The champion’s lay on hands also acts as sanctuary, using the champion’s level as the caster level. The saving throw DC to negate this effect is equal to 10 + 1/2 the champion’s level + the champion’s Charisma modifier. At 9th level, a champion adds the following mercies to the list of those that can be selected.
Confused: The target is no longer confused.
Cursed: The champion’s lay on hands ability also acts as remove curse, using the champion’s level as the caster level.
Exhausted: The target is no longer exhausted. The champion must have the fatigue mercy before selecting this mercy.
Frightened: The target is no longer frightened. The champion must have the shaken mercy before selecting this mercy.
Injured: The target gains fast healing 3 for a number of rounds equal to 1/2 the champion’s level.
Nauseated: The target is no longer nauseated. The champion must have the sickened mercy before selecting this mercy.
Poisoned: The champion’s lay on hands ability also acts as neutralize poison, using the champion’s level as the caster level.
Restorative: The target heals 1d4 points of ability damage from a single ability score of the champion’s choosing. The champion must have the enfeebled mercy before selecting this mercy. These abilities are cumulative. For example, a 9th-level champion’s lay on hands ability heals 4d6 points of damage and might also cure Fatigued and Exhausted conditions as well as removing diseases. Once a condition or spell effect is chosen, it can’t be changed.
Channel Energy: When a champion reaches 4th level, she gains the supernatural ability to channel energy like a cleric. Using this ability consumes two uses of her lay on hands ability. A champion uses her level as her effective cleric level when channeling positive energy. This is a Charisma-based ability.
Guardian Sight (Ex and Sp)

At 5th level you gain darkvision with a range of 120 feet. At 8th level you gain All-Around Vision; you can see in all directions at once and you can’t be flanked. At 11th level you are constantly under the effects of see invisibility.

Greater Smite (Su)

At 7th level the damage from the champion’s smite enemy ability increases to 3 extra points per champion level.
